note: Lightweight research manifest for a small first source/rights audit, corrected in 01B and reviewed for residual evidence wording by Codex. Rights labels summarize cited institutional statements, not global legal clearance. This is NOT the final ColorVerse corpus interchange schema described in docs/color-corpus-integration-assessment.md section E, and no entry here is an approved product record, approved palette, or approved color. Full source detail, rights citations and reasoning live in docs/research/corpus-source-audit-01.md.
candidatesEmptyReason: The brief accepts an original numeric value in its own original space (e.g. Munsell notation or CIE xyY) and never requires HEX. The empty list here is not about HEX conversion: it is because no primary source's raw numeric table was actually fetched and read in this pass (two sources describe numeric data on their listing/abstract pages, but the raw files/centroid table themselves were not retrieved), and no other source has both authoritative numeric values and a clear reuse basis. See sourcesReviewed[].eligibleForCandidate and docs/research/corpus-source-audit-01.md for full per-source reasoning. An empty list here is an honest result, not a placeholder to be filled with invented or hand-converted values.

sourcesReviewed.title: Munsell Renotation Data
sourcesReviewed.institution: Munsell Color Science Laboratory, Rochester Institute of Technology
sourcesReviewed.numericDataSpace: Munsell hue/value/chroma with CIE xyY (Illuminant C, CIE 1931 2-degree observer)
sourcesReviewed.reason: Hosting/listing page offers the files with no explicit reuse license (paraphrased: distributed as-is, no license grant stated). Reuse basis is unresolved, and the raw real.dat/all.dat/1929.dat tables were not actually fetched or read in this pass (direct fetch of the data-file host returned HTTP 403), so no specific xyY value has been verified. The brief does not require HEX; original Munsell/xyY values could be a valid future candidate once both the license is resolved and the raw values are actually read.

sourcesReviewed.title: Color: Universal Language and Dictionary of Names (NBS Special Publication 440)
sourcesReviewed.institution: U.S. National Bureau of Standards (Kelly & Judd, 1976)
sourcesReviewed.numericDataSpace: Munsell notation centroids/ranges for 267 ISCC-NBS color-name blocks (not sRGB/HEX)
sourcesReviewed.reason: Government-authored text is public domain in the United States according to the cited NIST policy (17 U.S.C. 105); embedded third-party material and other territories are not cleared by this statement. The brief does not require converting Munsell-notation centroids to HEX; the actual reason no candidate was taken from this source is that the centroid table inside the scanned PDF was not actually fetched and read in this pass (it exceeded this session's fetch size limit), so no specific centroid value has been verified against the primary document.

sourcesReviewed.title: CIE 015:2018, Colorimetry (4th edition)
sourcesReviewed.reason: Confirmed as a paid standard sold via the CIE Webshop and National Committees; not a color list. Being sold confirms it is not freely available, but its actual license/redistribution terms were not fetched or read, so they are not independently verified. Cited only as methodology background.

sourcesReviewed.title: Color Standards and Color Nomenclature
sourcesReviewed.institution: Robert Ridgway, 1912; digitized by Smithsonian Libraries and Archives
sourcesReviewed.reason: 53 printed pigment plates with 1,115 named colors, but no colorimetric measurement data accompanies them. A scan's RGB pixels are not the historical original per the task brief, so no HEX values were extracted. (A secondary-source claim about influencing later commercial color systems was found but not independently verified, so it is not repeated here.)

sourcesReviewed.title: Werner's Nomenclature of Colours (1821 edition, arranged by Patrick Syme)
sourcesReviewed.institution: Smithsonian Libraries and Archives (digitized copy on Internet Archive)
sourcesReviewed.reason: Hand-painted watercolor swatches only, no colorimetric measurement data. Modern popular reinterpretations exist elsewhere but are separate secondary works, not this primary 1821 source, and were not used as evidence.

sourcesReviewed.title: A Dictionary of Color Combinations / Haishoku Sokan (配色総鑑)
sourcesReviewed.reason: Do not apply today's life-plus-70 term retroactively: Japan's official Agency for Cultural Affairs Q&A confirms the 2018 term-extension reform does not revive a copyright that had already expired before it took effect (2018-12-30). This audit does not determine the expiry date or legal treatment of this particular work; author-life-date authority records, edition-specific material and territory-specific status require further verification. Status is therefore unresolved, not verified-restricted and not free-to-use; edition- and territory-specific clearance is required. No colorimetric data was found. The separate task rule against bulk Wada ingestion remains regardless of rights status; this entry is for research only, not proposed for use.
